title: The trade you will not take
situation: After two losing demo trades this week, you see a setup that meets every rule in your plan. Your [[stop-loss|stop loss]] and size are already worked out, and the risk is within your own limit. But your finger hovers over the button and you do not take it.
question: What do you do?

responses.text: Skip it. It feels safer not to trade until you feel confident again.
responses.explanation: Skipping avoids a possible loss, but your results stop reflecting your plan. You also learn nothing about whether the plan works.

responses.text: Take it, but with a stop so tight that price can barely move.
responses.explanation: A stop placed out of fear, not where the setup needs it, is likely to be hit by normal price movement.

responses.text: Wait for extra confirmation beyond your rules, then enter late.
responses.explanation: Waiting longer changes your entry and your reward compared with your risk. You are no longer trading the plan you tested.

responses.text: Take the trade as planned. The risk is set, and a loss here is a cost you accepted in advance.
responses.explanation: Your plan already decided how much you can lose. Following it is how you find out whether the plan works.

takeaway: When the risk is set in advance, following the plan matters more than how the trade feels.
